title: The physical location of SNAP enrollment offices changes participation in nearby places
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34529, The Intersection of Place and Need: How Lack of Enrollment Offices Deters Participation in the Safety Net
geography: United States; administrative SNAP participation and geocoded enrollment offices in one state, with census-tract event-study comparisons

observations.period: Office openings and closures; study's administrative event-study period

denominator.unit: single-state SNAP administrative dataset linked to geocoded enrollment-office locations; effects estimated at census-tract level

office_closure_effect.unit: SNAP participation in a census tract over two years following an enrollment-office closure

observations.method: Authors link administrative SNAP receipt data to geocoded enrollment-office locations and use event-study designs around frequent office openings and closings, with robustness checks for alternative specifications and endogeneity in office placement.
observations.uncertainty: The study covers one state and measures area-level participation, not every eligible household's application attempt, benefit adequacy, food security, travel time, or later household outcome. The estimate is tied to the study's design, period, and administrative records.
observations.subgroup: Census tracts near opening or closing offices, with effects reported as concentrated in urban areas; individual household mechanisms are not fully observed in the summary.
observations.counterinterpretation: Office closure may coincide with broader administrative or neighborhood changes, although the authors report robustness checks addressing endogeneity; remote, mobile, telephone, or alternative enrollment routes may offset some effects.

related_sources.claim: NBER paper reports the administrative data, geocoded office linkage, event-study design, 7–9% closure estimate, suggestive opening effect, and urban concentration.

boundary: This record establishes a causal place-to-program-participation link in one state's SNAP system. It does not establish a national effect, household food security, benefit adequacy, application effort, remote-access substitution, or later political or health outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: NBER Working Paper 34529 PDF retrieved and hashed; individual administrative records and restricted geocoded office data not retained
